review.summary:
changes_needed
Fan-in instructions reverse the accepted conflict-before-quorum correction.
The provenance hook admits document values and can retain evidence across runs.
The A2A sketch duplicates tasks on resume and mishandles results.
Checks: 27 tests passed; link checker reported bad 0.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: contradictions between lessons and worked answers
findings.title: Remove conflicted votes before checking the quorum
findings.claim: The integrative exercise explicitly puts quorum before conflict removal, reversing the accepted correction in 8.3. The recap at line 926 repeats this order, and quiz answer 3 omits conflict removal entirely.
findings.evidence: The new order is 'provenance → group by scope → 3-of-5 quorum → conflicts to escalation'. Executing 8.3's corrected merge with two clean confirmations and a third site reporting both confirmed and rejected gives fleet_ticket=False; counting confirmations before excluding that conflict gives True.
findings.proposed_change: Use 'provenance → group by (scope, hypothesis) → escalate and exclude conflicting groups → quorum → sorted output' consistently in the recap, quiz answer and integrative exercise. Verify with two clean sites plus one conflicted site: no fleet ticket.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: code sketches must implement the lesson's guard
findings.title: Limit provenance evidence to trusted data tools within one run
findings.claim: The recorder accepts numbers from every ops tool, including document-reading tools, rather than enforcing the established exclusion of document and extractor values. The shared seen set can also authorize a value from an earlier run when hooks are reused.
findings.evidence: Executing these hooks with a matching mcp__ops__archive_read_doc result containing 38 makes provenance accept deciding_value=38. Reusing the hooks for another run with no data-tool calls also accepts 38. Week 5's dated correction and PROJ-2026-10-27-F2 explicitly exclude archive and extractor results.
findings.proposed_change: Create the evidence set and hooks per run, and record only an explicit allow-list of trusted measurement tools. Exclude archive, extractor and ticket outputs. Check that a document-only value and a previous run's value are denied, while a current-run measurement is allowed; retain the earlier bare-number matching caveat.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: code sketches must match resumability claims
findings.title: Reuse the saved remote task when the executor resumes
findings.claim: The executor always sends a new message and overwrites the saved task id. It never reads the checkpointed mapping, so restarting this sketch duplicates the remote task despite the lesson's explicit resume requirement.
findings.evidence: Running the extracted sketch twice with the same block.id and checkpoint produced two send_message calls; st.remote['tu_1'] changed from task '1' to task '2'. Line 383 instead says to get the stored task on resume, and the exercise requires exactly one remote task after restart.
findings.proposed_change: First look up block.id in st.remote. Fetch that task if present; only send and checkpoint a new task when no mapping exists. Run the exercise's crash-during-polling case and assert one send_message call across both processes.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: API data shapes and executable sketches
findings.title: Read structured data from artifact parts
findings.claim: An A2A artifact contains parts; it does not expose the structured result directly as artifact.data. The sketch therefore fails on the successful mixed data-and-text artifact required by exercise (c).
findings.evidence: The official specification defines Artifact.parts and places data on a Part: https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/ . Running the sketch with an artifact containing a data part and a text part raises AttributeError at task.artifacts[0].data. The lesson's own object definitions also say artifacts are made of parts.
findings.proposed_change: Select the expected structured data part from the artifact's parts and pass that part's data to QAFacts.model_validate. Demonstrate exercise (c): null_rate=0.31 is returned and the instruction-bearing text part is excluded.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: guards and terminal-state handling
findings.title: Distinguish paused, failed and successful A2A tasks
findings.claim: Only INPUT_REQUIRED reaches the durable gate. AUTH_REQUIRED keeps polling until cancellation, while FAILED, CANCELED and REJECTED fall through to successful-result parsing. This contradicts the state descriptions and diagram.
findings.evidence: With the states listed at line 358, a stub AUTH_REQUIRED task repeatedly called get_task without returning pending. A FAILED task with no artifacts exited the loop and raised IndexError. A failed task carrying a partial artifact could instead be rendered as a successful answer.
findings.proposed_change: Route both required states to the appropriate durable pending gate. Parse result artifacts only for COMPLETED; map the other terminal states to explicit unsuccessful outcomes. Verify AUTH_REQUIRED pauses and failed, canceled and rejected tasks never produce a successful answer.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: arithmetic and worked answers
findings.title: Account for the confirmation removed by the signature lock
findings.claim: The answer asserts three independent confirmations after collapsing two workers, but the fixture does not identify those workers or explain how their independent evidence survives. A permitted collision between two otherwise confirming W2 workers leaves only two confirmations.
findings.evidence: Dropping PVA-01's orphan and timing out PVA-06 leaves PVA-02, PVA-04 and PVA-05. If PVA-02 and PVA-04 collapse into one investigation, only two independent confirming investigations remain. No replacement check or evidence-preserving mechanism is described, yet the answer files the fleet ticket.
findings.proposed_change: Add a dated correction explaining the ambiguity. Specify the colliding workers and show how three distinct site confirmations are independently obtained, or show the quorum failing when only two remain. Shared evidence must not be counted twice as independent confirmation.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: arithmetic and coverage claims
findings.title: Do not equate random test samples with complete coverage
findings.claim: Different random samples across sixteen agents do not establish that the fleet covers every test. The statement overstates the guarantee provided by the described fast mode.
findings.evidence: With sixteen fixed 1% samples, their union covers at most 16% of the suite, even without overlap. Fixed 10% samples can overlap and also do not guarantee complete coverage. The paragraph explicitly says each agent repeats the same sample.
findings.proposed_change: Qualify the claim: different samples broaden fleet coverage but do not guarantee every test is exercised. If the source describes a separate complete-suite run, distinguish it from fast-mode sampling; otherwise preserve the source wording with a dated mathematical caveat.
